decisions.reason: Restricting ESP32 GPIO35, GPIO36, and GPIO37 does not change the named interboard signals, connector selection, or connector pinout.
The GPIO restrictions do not change the I2C cable, speed, pull-up, or series-resistor requirements.
The interboard power connector and matching pin-order rule do not depend on GPIO35, GPIO36, or GPIO37.
The restriction does not change the requirement to provide native USB D+ and D- data lines.
Avoiding three GPIO numbers does not alter the three-board architecture or the defined roles of the main and sensor boards.
The restricted GPIO numbers do not affect the standalone USB power regulator, activation condition, powered loads, or source-selection behavior.
The LED interface state specifies 5V power, level shifting, and GPIO3-controlled shutdown; none uses GPIO35, GPIO36, or GPIO37.
The switched 5V rail uses GPIO5 at the source time, so restricting GPIO35, GPIO36, and GPIO37 does not change its state.
The sensor board's role as a connector hub remains unchanged and has no specified dependency on the restricted GPIO numbers.
The sleep and wake requirement uses GPIO26 for touch wake and does not assign GPIO35, GPIO36, or GPIO37.
The restriction does not change the requirement for an eight-addressable-LED board.
The GPIO restrictions do not affect the deferred requirement for JLCPCB-compatible LCSC part numbers in the BOM.
